about:
# Hearthtale

Hearthtale keeps a journal for your World of Warcraft character as you play.
Quests, close calls, new places and the people you travel with become entries
written in your character's voice. Each race has its own way of telling the
story. On Hardcore, a death closes the journal with an epitaph and saves it
in the Hall of the Fallen.

You can read the books in game or on **[hearthtale.app](https://hearthtale.app/)**.
The optional [Ravenpost](https://ravenpost-site.vercel.app/) companion
uploads them after you log out or reload.

For Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery and World of Warcraft:
Forever. One download covers both games.

## In game

Type `/hearthtale` or `/ht`, or click the minimap button to open the journal.
Each login says in chat whether you're resuming an entry or starting a new
one.
Choose an entry from the list to read it. The second tab holds the Hall of
the Fallen, which you can also open with `/ht hall`. The third holds your
fellow travellers: the players you have grouped with, when and where you met,
the days you spent together, and a note of your own on each. They stay on your
computer, never in the book or on the site.

An entry follows the time between rests. Logging out at an inn, in a city
or by a campfire closes it. Logging out in the wild records a night outdoors
and keeps it going. After four hours of play, the next logout closes the entry
wherever you are. A character you already play starts with a prologue, then
builds a journal from that point on.

Use an entry's **Edit** button to give it your own title or add a note. You
can also use `/ht title [N] TEXT` and `/ht note [N] TEXT`. Leave out N to
change the latest entry. Your words are kept separately from the journal's
text.

A finished entry keeps its words, even after an update improves the
writing. `/ht rewrite` writes the whole journal again with the current
version, after asking. Your titles and notes stay.

## Read on hearthtale.app

Install Ravenpost and click **Sign in with Battle.net** in its window. For
Forever characters, or any character Battle.net cannot find, get
a code from **Link a character** on the site and enter `/ht link CODE` in
game. Your book arrives after your next logout or `/reload`.

The website is optional, and books are private unless you choose to share
them. Your notes stay out of a shared book and the Hall. Setup instructions
are at [hearthtale.app/start](https://hearthtale.app/start).

The interface is available in English and French.

The journal is written in English, on any game client. On other clients the
game's names in it (places, creatures, people, quests, items, trades, spells)
are kept in English too. In Forever dungeons, the journal can
only tell kills that a quest also counts.

## Settings

The welcome page appears once per character. Open it again with
`/ht welcome`. Settings are under **Options > AddOns > Hearthtale**, through
`/ht settings` or by right-clicking the minimap button.

Choose the alert when a book closes and the minimap button's visibility and
position (chat lines always show). You can mark a character as Hardcore when
the game cannot identify it. Settings are saved per character and can be
transferred with `/ht export` and `/ht import CODE`. Use `/ht minimap` to
show or hide the button.

The settings also offer the book's size (four steps) and paper colours (dark ink on tan paper, applied by a
reload: the page ends with a Reload button). **Options > Key Bindings** lists **Open Hearthtale**: one key,
or on Forever a controller button, opens and closes the journal. Nothing is bound until you choose.

Hearthtale shares its book style with its author's other addons, listed on
its store page. Each addon works independently.

The full store description is in [addon/CURSEFORGE.md](https://github.com/salty-max/hearthtale/blob/main/addon/CURSEFORGE.md).
[PLAN.md](https://github.com/salty-max/hearthtale/blob/main/PLAN.md) records the design decisions, and [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/salty-max/hearthtale/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)
describes how the journal is written and the rules its sentences follow.

## Development

The addon lives in `addon/`, with its writing in `writing/`.

```bash
bun run addon:build     # Build Data_Classic.lua and Data_Forever.lua
bun run addon:check     # Check generated files, simulations, writing and samples
bun run addon:package   # Create dist/Hearthtale-<version>.zip
bun run addon:seed      # Generate test characters and website samples
bun run addon:golden save    # Save journal output before a writer refactor
bun run addon:golden check   # Compare output after the refactor
bun run audit           # Check game data and play through each race's quests
```

The website lives in `apps/` and `packages/`. Run `bun install` once before
starting it.

```bash
bun run db             # Start local Postgres on port 5435
bun run db:migrate
bun run db:seed         # Load the test characters
bun run dev            # API on port 3002, web on port 5175
bun run check          # Run addon checks, typechecking, lint and tests
```

The local site has a **Use the test account** button. The API uses Hono on
Bun with Postgres and Drizzle. The web app uses React, Vite and Tailwind, and
can be installed as a PWA. Shared data types live in `packages/shared`.
The site is hosted on Vercel with Neon.

To release the addon, run
`scripts/release.sh --version X.Y.Z [--hold] NOTES.md`. The script tags and
pushes the release, and GitHub Actions publishes it on GitHub, CurseForge
and Wago.

## License

[GPL-3.0-or-later](https://github.com/salty-max/hearthtale/blob/main/LICENSE). The game data comes through
[wow-data](https://github.com/salty-max/wow-data): the game clients' tables on
[wago.tools](https://wago.tools/), [QuestieDB](https://github.com/Questie/QuestieDB)
and [cmangos classic-db](https://github.com/cmangos/classic-db) (GPL-3.0). The
names themselves belong to Blizzard.

Forever's own quests in `addon/Hearthtale/Forever.lua` also draw on
[AllTheThings](https://github.com/ATTWoWAddon/AllTheThings) (MIT) for their
rewards and prerequisites, [Wowhead](https://www.wowhead.com/forever)'s Forever
pages for their texts, levels and givers (what each quest was for, in
`writing/why/`, is written from those texts) and the facts players share. Not
affiliated with Blizzard Entertainment.

releases.notes:
Hearthtale 0.15.0

- New: **Book size** makes the whole window larger, in four steps from Normal to Largest, and **Paper colours** show dark ink on tan paper instead of the dark look. Both are in the settings. Paper colours apply after a reload, and the settings page now ends with a Reload button and a line saying so.
- New: a key binding. **Options > Key Bindings** lists **Open Hearthtale** under a heading of its own, so one key, or on Forever a controller button, opens and closes the journal. Nothing is bound until you choose.
- On Forever, the window now tells the Gamepad UI that it is open, so a controller's D-pad can move across its buttons.
- On Forever with the Gamepad UI on, the game can show its blocked-action popup after an options page opens. That is a bug in the game's own Gamepad UI. A reload clears it, and the settings page now says so.
- The game's data is brought up to date.

More fixes for Forever.

- On Forever the game sometimes hides a name, a class or a character's identity. The diary now leaves that line out and carries on, instead of raising an error.
- A group member's class and a journal that begins under a hidden identity are handled the same way.

Fixes for Forever's launch.

- Spells the Forever client removed before launch (Salvation, Blessing of Light, Revoke and a few more) still read by name in your diary.
- The diary no longer risks an error when the game hides the quest giver's name or your specialisation.

Fixes for Forever's launch.

- Spells the Forever client removed before launch (Salvation, Blessing of Light, Revoke and a few more) still read by name in your diary.
- The diary no longer risks an error when the game hides the quest giver's name or your specialisation.

Hearthtale 0.14.0

- New: the journal can be written in French. A character's journal starts in the language of the game client at its first login, French on a French client and English on any other, and keeps it.
- New: a Journal language setting changes it, and the whole journal is written again in the other language.
- The French journal has its own words for every deed, the race voices, and the game's own names for places, creatures, people and clans.
- The French words ship as a second folder, Hearthtale_French, loaded only when a journal is written in French.
- On hearthtale.app, a book is shown in its own language, French or English, and the site itself speaks French when your browser does.
